step1.description: Send the check-in/check-out template and wait for the button reply. The button id (CLOCK_IN / CLOCK_OUT) is captured directly as this step's logType.

step2.description: Send the shift list built from the employee's real assigned shifts (system.shiftOptions, populated from AgentProcessParams.shiftDetails) and wait for the pick. This is the one case the pipeline does not template: the row COUNT varies per employee (some have 2 shifts, some 5), and a template's listSections is a fixed set of rows — nothing can add or remove one per send, so send_list_whatsapp_message stays here regardless of the all-templates rule. Any valid shift falls through to defaults.onUnrelated since the choice itself doesn't branch the flow. Each list item's id is the composite 'shiftId|shiftName' string; captureFields splits it back into state.step2.shiftId / state.step2.shiftName on the way out — no onButton map needed since the option ids are dynamic per employee.

step3.description: Ask for the current location and wait for the shared location. This is the other case the pipeline does not template: a location-share prompt needs messageType 'location', and no InteractiveType or template field can express that — so send_whatsapp_message stays here regardless of the all-templates rule. Location is a structural message kind, so it always advances via 'next' rather than a router.

params.message: 📍 Please share your current location to mark your attendance.

step3.unexpectedTypeMessage: Please share your current location using WhatsApp's attachment (📎) button.

step4.description: Mark the attendance and end the flow. handle_location_message validates the shared location, persists the check-in/out, and sends its own confirmation message — no further step needed after this.
